props.gloss_en: R' Yehuda would concede to the Rabbis on olives and grapes [what seeps from them is forbidden even if brought in for food]
and the Rabbis would concede to R' Yehuda on other fruit [what seeps from fruit brought in for food is permitted]
R' Yirmeya to R' Abba: then about what do they disagree?
R' Abba: when you find it [you will know]
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it stands to reason that they disagree about mulberries and pomegranates
olives from which one drew oil and grapes from which one drew wine, brought in whether for food or for liquid -- what comes out of them is forbidden
mulberries and pomegranates from which one drew juice, brought in for food -- what comes out of them is permitted
brought in for liquid -- what comes out is forbidden
brought in without specification -- what comes out is forbidden; the words of R' Yehuda
the Rabbis: whether for food or for liquid, what comes out of them is forbidden
a woman's milk renders susceptible [to impurity] whether willed or unwilled
an animal's milk renders susceptible only when willed
the Sages: baskets of olives and grapes will prove it -- the liquids coming from them willed are impure, unwilled are pure
(entertained) 'willed' is where he is pleased; 'unwilled' is where he expressed nothing
no: 'willed' includes the unspecified; 'unwilled' is where he revealed his mind, saying 'I do not want it'
baskets of olives and grapes are different: since [that liquid] stands to be lost, he renounces it from the outset
one may squeeze plums, quinces and crab apples
but not pomegranates
and those of the house of Menashya bar Menachem would squeeze pomegranates
since they are not [fruits] made for squeezing, [squeezing is permitted] even ab initio -- on R' Yehuda's view and on the Rabbis' alike
Rav Nachman: the halakha follows [the practice of] the house of Menashya bar Menachem [squeezing pomegranates is forbidden]
one who maintains thorns in a vineyard -- R' Eliezer: he has sanctified [the vineyard as kilayim]
the Sages: only a thing whose like people maintain sanctifies
R' Chanina: R' Eliezer's reason is that in Arabia they maintain field thorns for their camels
Rav Chisda: beets one squeezed and put into a mikveh disqualify the mikveh by change of colour
but beets are not made for squeezing! rather, since he valued them, they became liquid
here too [the pomegranates of Beit Menashya], since he valued them, they became liquid
Rav Pappa: [beets disqualify] because they are a thing from which a mikveh is not made ab initio
and whatever a mikveh is not made from ab initio disqualifies the mikveh by change of colour
the mishna there: if wine, vinegar or mochal fell into it and changed its colour -- [the mikveh] is invalid
Abaye: the tanna who holds mochal is liquid [and so the mishna] is R' Yaakov
R' Yaakov: mochal is like liquid
and why did they say the mochal that comes out at first is pure? because he does not want it to remain
R' Shimon: mochal is not like liquid
and why did they say the mochal coming from the press-bale is impure? because it cannot be without drops of oil
what is between them? mochal that comes after the heavy pressing
Rava: [mochal disqualifies] because it is a thing from which a mikveh is not made, and [such a thing] disqualifies the mikveh by change of colour
a person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot [of food]
but not into a bowl
Rav Chisda: from our master's words we learn -- a person may milk a goat into a pot, but not into a bowl
evidently he holds: liquid that comes into food is food
a zav who milks a goat -- the milk is impure
R' Yochanan: [it is made susceptible] by the drop smeared on the mouth of the teat
one corpse-impure who squeezed olives and grapes, exactly an egg-bulk -- [the liquid] is pure; hence more than an egg-bulk -- impure
R' Yirmeya: [the question whether liquid that comes into food is food] is a tannaitic dispute -- the smoothing-with-grapes mishna
one who smooths [bread] with grapes -- it is not made susceptible
R' Yehuda: it is made susceptible
do they not disagree over this -- one holds liquid that comes into food is food, the other that it is not?
Rav Pappa: all agree that liquid that comes into food is not food
and here they disagree over liquid that goes to waste -- one holds it is liquid, the other that it is not
Rav Pappa: and they disagree [as] in the dispute of these tannaim -- the olive-cutting baraita
one who cuts olives with impure hands -- [they are] made susceptible
[cutting them] to dip them in salt -- not made susceptible
to learn whether his olives have reached harvest or not -- not made susceptible
R' Yehuda: made susceptible
do they not disagree over this -- one holds liquid standing to go to waste is liquid, the other that it is not?
Rav Huna b. Rav Yehoshua: and those tannaim [of the smoothing mishna] disagree over liquid that stands to polish [the bread]
and a fish for its brine [may be squeezed] even into a bowl
pickled vegetables one squeezed: for themselves -- permitted
for their water -- exempt but forbidden
Rav: and boiled vegetables, whether for themselves or for their water -- permitted
Shmuel: pickled and boiled alike -- for themselves permitted, for their water exempt but forbidden
Rav Dimi: by God! 'my eyes have seen and not a stranger' (Job 19:27) -- I heard it from the mouth of R' Yirmeya [and so back to Rav]

schemas.gloss_en: woman's milk, made only for infants, renders susceptible willed or unwilled; animal's milk, made for infants and adults -- is it not logical that it renders susceptible willed or unwilled?

grounds.gloss_en: the Sages (אמרו לו): if a woman's milk renders susceptible unwilled, that is because the blood of her wound is impure; shall animal milk, whose wound's blood is pure?

answered_by.gloss_en: מחמיר אני בחלב מבדם -- one who milks for healing, [the milk] is impure; one who lets blood for healing, [the blood] is pure

grounds.gloss_en: the Sages (אמרו לו): סלי זיתים וענבים יוכיחו -- the liquids from them are impure when willed and pure when unwilled (= p_salim_leratzon); a liquid can render susceptible only when willed, so animal milk may be such a liquid. Unanswered.

schemas.gloss_en: olives and grapes, which are made for squeezing -- unwilled [seepage] is nothing; mulberries and pomegranates, not made for squeezing, all the more so

grounds.gloss_en: לא: 'willed' is the unspecified case and 'unwilled' is where he said 'I do not want it' -- the baskets say nothing about the unspecified case
ואיבעית אימא: baskets of olives and grapes are different -- their liquid stands to be lost, so he renounces it from the outset

supports.gloss_en: דתניא -- the baraita sets R' Yehuda (mulberries and pomegranates for food: permitted) against the Rabbis (forbidden), and has R' Yehuda forbid olives and grapes either way
אשכחן רבי יהודה דמודי לרבנן בזיתים ובענבים -- from the baraita's olives and grapes clause
רבנן דמודו ליה לרבי יהודה בשאר פירות מנלן? דתניא: סוחטין בפגעין ובפרישין ובעוזרדין, אבל לא ברמונים

deflected_by.gloss_en: וממאי דרבנן היא? דילמא רבי יהודה היא -- perhaps the baraita is R' Yehuda's, and shows nothing about the Rabbis

refuted_by.gloss_en: R' Yehuda was heard only on what seeps by itself; squeezing ab initio is permitted only because they are not made for squeezing -- and that holds for the Rabbis too: שמע מינה רבנן היא, שמע מינה

supports.gloss_en: אין, דתנן: R' Eliezer's thorns sanctify a vineyard because in Arabia they keep thorns for camels -- a practice not universal still counts

deflected_by.gloss_en: מידי איריא? Arabia is a place; here his view is nullified beside all other people

supports.gloss_en: אלא היינו טעמא כדרב חסדא -- beets are not made for squeezing yet their juice, valued, is liquid; so the pomegranates
דתניא, רבי יעקב אומר: מוחל הרי הוא כמשקה
מדברי רבינו נלמד -- as a cluster may be squeezed into a pot, so a goat may be milked into a pot
אלמא קסבר -- since into a pot is permitted and into a bowl is not, liquid that comes into food is food
מאי לאו בהא קמיפלגי -- one holds liquid that comes into food is food, the other not
מאי לאו בהא קמיפלגי -- one holds liquid standing to go to waste is liquid, the other not

objections.gloss_en: וסבר רבי יהודה סתם אסור? והתנן -- the milk mishna's baskets of olives and grapes: unwilled seepage does not render susceptible; if that means the unspecified case, then a fortiori for mulberries and pomegranates (kv_salim_tutim)

answered_by.gloss_en: לא: 'unwilled' is where he revealed his mind -- 'I do not want it' (= p_shelo_leratzon_gilui_daat)
ואיבעית אימא: the baskets are different -- liquid standing to be lost he renounces from the outset (= p_salim_leibud_mafkir)

objections.gloss_en: מנשיא בן מנחם תנא הוא?! and if the halakha follows the tanna who held like him -- because he held like him, does the halakha follow him? is Menashya ben Menachem the majority of the world?

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא היינו טעמא כדרב חסדא -- squeezed beets disqualify a mikveh though not made for squeezing, since he valued them; here too, the pomegranates he valued are liquid (= p_hacha_nami_ahshevinhu)

objections.gloss_en: a zav who milks a goat -- the milk is impure; and if liquid that comes into food is food, with what was it made susceptible?

answered_by.gloss_en: כדאמר רבי יוחנן: by the drop smeared on the mouth of the teat; here too (= p_ryochanan_tipa)

objections.gloss_en: one corpse-impure who squeezed olives and grapes: more than an egg-bulk -- impure; and if liquid that comes into food is food, with what was it made susceptible?

answered_by.gloss_en: הוא מותיב לה והוא מפרק לה: where he squeezes into a bowl

objections.gloss_en: מי אמר שמואל דג לצירו אפילו לתוך הקערה? והאיתמר: Shmuel -- pickled and boiled alike, for their water, exempt but forbidden (amoraic-memra contradiction; no objection kind of its own)

answered_by.gloss_en: האלהים! עיני ראו ולא זר -- I heard it from R' Yirmeya, he from R' Zeira, he from Rav Chiyya bar Ashi, he from Rav: it is Rav's ruling, not Shmuel's (= p_einai_rau)
